section: Forest and wildlife legal framework - Indian Forest Act 1927, Forest (Conservation) Act 1980, Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972
subsections: Related provisions - list placement, Godavarman, NBWL chair
Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972 - year, subject-matter, ownership, hunting
Biological Diversity Act 2002 - structure, PBR, BHS
Authorities under wildlife and biodiversity laws

accepted.s:
The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 transferred which of the following subjects from the State List to the Concurrent List?
1. Forests
2. Protection of wild animals and birds
3. Public health
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The 42nd Amendment transferred forests through Entry 17A and protection of wild animals and birds through Entry 17B to the Concurrent List. Public health was not transferred by this amendment.
accepted.tq: Identify the two related entries and reject the unrelated subject.
accepted.sec: Related provisions - list placement, Godavarman, NBWL chair

accepted.s: Which one of the following provisions was inserted into the Directive Principles of State Policy by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976?
accepted.x: Article 48A, directing the State to protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife, was inserted by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.
accepted.tq: Use the constitutional-part distinction to separate a DPSP from a Fundamental Duty.
accepted.sec: Related provisions - list placement, Godavarman, NBWL chair

accepted.s: Article 51A(g), relating to protection of the natural environment, belongs to which part of the Constitution?
accepted.x: Article 51A(g) is a Fundamental Duty requiring citizens to protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the similarly related Articles 48A and 51A(g).
accepted.sec: Related provisions - list placement, Godavarman, NBWL chair

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the T.N. Godavarman Thirumulpad case:
1. The expression ‘forest’ covers every area recorded as forest in government records.
2. The definition applies irrespective of ownership.
3. The interpretation is confined only to notified national parks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Godavarman interpretation covers every area recorded as forest in government records, regardless of ownership. It is not confined to national parks.
accepted.tq: Find the incorrect limiting statement.
accepted.sec: Related provisions - list placement, Godavarman, NBWL chair

accepted.s: Who chairs the National Board for Wildlife?
accepted.x: The National Board for Wildlife is chaired by the Prime Minister. Its Standing Committee is chaired by the Union Environment Minister.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who chairs this body?’ authority trap.
accepted.sec: Related provisions - list placement, Godavarman, NBWL chair

accepted.s: The Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife is chaired by the:
o: Chief Minister of the concerned State
accepted.x: The Standing Committee of the NBWL is chaired by the Union Environment Minister and considers projects in or near protected areas and tiger corridors.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the chairperson of the parent body from that of its Standing Committee.
accepted.sec: Related provisions - list placement, Godavarman, NBWL chair

accepted.s:
The Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife is concerned, among other matters, with projects located in or near:
1. Protected areas
2. Tiger corridors
3. Municipal corporation areas without any wildlife connection
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Standing Committee clears or considers projects in or near protected areas and tiger corridors. Municipal corporation areas as such are not the specified category.
accepted.tq: Reject the unrelated location added to a pair of connected functions.
accepted.sec: Related provisions - list placement, Godavarman, NBWL chair

accepted.s: The Supreme Court’s restriction relating to mining provides that mining is barred within what distance of every national park and sanctuary, unless a larger eco-sensitive zone is notified?
accepted.x: Mining is barred within 1 kilometre of every national park and sanctuary boundary unless a larger eco-sensitive zone is notified.
accepted.tq: Recall the statutory-distance figure and distinguish it from larger possible buffer zones.
accepted.sec: Related provisions - list placement, Godavarman, NBWL chair

accepted.s: Under Section 39 of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, wild animals, trophies and articles derived from wild animals are treated as:
o: Property of the local body where found
Property of the State Government only
accepted.x: Section 39 declares wild animals, trophies and articles derived from them to be Government property.
accepted.tq: Test ownership through the exact statutory authority rather than the place of discovery.
accepted.sec: Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972 - year, subject-matter, ownership, hunting

accepted.s: Which of the following amendments to the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 is NOT included among the amendments identified in the subject matter?
accepted.x: The identified amendments were made in 1991, 2002, 2006 and 2022. A 2016 amendment is not included in this sequence.
accepted.tq: Find the one year outside the recognised amendment sequence.
accepted.sec: Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972 - year, subject-matter, ownership, hunting

accepted.s: Under Section 9 of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, hunting of scheduled animals is generally:
o: Permitted throughout the year with a licence
accepted.x: Section 9 prohibits hunting of scheduled animals, subject to exceptions provided by the Act.
accepted.tq: Look for the general rule together with its statutory qualification.
accepted.sec: Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972 - year, subject-matter, ownership, hunting

accepted.s: A scheduled wild animal is causing imminent danger to human life. Which provision may permit action against the animal?
accepted.x: Section 11 provides exceptions to the prohibition on hunting, including situations involving danger to human life or crops.
accepted.tq: Apply the exception to the general prohibition in a practical situation.
accepted.sec: Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972 - year, subject-matter, ownership, hunting

accepted.s:
Permits under Section 12 of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 may be granted for:
1. Education and research
2. Scientific management
3. Translocation
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Section 12 permits specified activities including education, research, scientific management and translocation.
accepted.tq: Select the complete list of statutory purposes.
accepted.sec: Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972 - year, subject-matter, ownership, hunting

accepted.s: Which of the following is the correct sequence of the three principal pillars of the Biological Diversity Act framework?
o: Hunting control, mining regulation and pollution taxation
Conservation, sustainable use and Access and Benefit Sharing
accepted.x: The Biological Diversity Act implements the Convention on Biological Diversity through conservation, sustainable use and Access and Benefit Sharing.
accepted.tq: Identify the recognised three-pillar framework instead of related but non-equivalent activities.
accepted.sec: Biological Diversity Act 2002 - structure, PBR, BHS

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Institution)
a. National Biodiversity Authority
b. State Biodiversity Boards
c. Biodiversity Management Committees
List-II (Principal role)
i. Preparation of People’s Biodiversity Registers
ii. Regulation of commercial use by Indian entities
iii. Regulation and approvals for foreign entities

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: The NBA regulates and approves activities involving foreign entities, State Biodiversity Boards regulate commercial use by Indian entities, and local BMCs prepare PBRs.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure local-body and PBR pair, then complete the institutional hierarchy.
accepted.sec: Biological Diversity Act 2002 - structure, PBR, BHS

accepted.s: Approximately how many People’s Biodiversity Registers had been prepared as of June 2026?
accepted.x: Approximately 2.72 lakh People’s Biodiversity Registers had been prepared as of June 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the updated figure from the earlier 1.5 lakh and the BMC count.
accepted.sec: Biological Diversity Act 2002 - structure, PBR, BHS

accepted.s: Biodiversity Heritage Sites are notified under Section 37 by the:
o: Central Government on the recommendation of the NBA alone
State Government on the recommendation of the State Biodiversity Board, in consultation with local bodies
accepted.x: The State Government notifies Biodiversity Heritage Sites under Section 37 on the recommendation of the State Biodiversity Board and in consultation with local bodies.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct authority and consultation chain.
accepted.sec: Biological Diversity Act 2002 - structure, PBR, BHS

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Biodiversity Heritage Sites is correct?
1. They may protect wild relatives of crops.
2. Traditional uses may continue in such sites.
3. They can be notified only by the Central Government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Biodiversity Heritage Sites may protect wild relatives of crops and allow traditional uses to continue. They are notified by State Governments, not only by the Central Government.
accepted.tq: Reject the wrong authority while retaining the two substantive features.
accepted.sec: Biological Diversity Act 2002 - structure, PBR, BHS

accepted.s: The State Board for Wildlife is chaired by the:
accepted.x: The State Board for Wildlife is chaired by the Chief Minister of the concerned State.
accepted.tq: Match the state-level body with the state political executive.
accepted.sec: Authorities under wildlife and biodiversity laws  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following authorities according to the years associated with their establishment or constitution, from earliest to latest:
A. Animal Welfare Board
B. National Biodiversity Authority
C. National Tiger Conservation Authority
D. Wildlife Crime Control Bureau
accepted.x: The relevant years are Animal Welfare Board—1962, National Biodiversity Authority—2003, National Tiger Conservation Authority—2006, and Wildlife Crime Control Bureau—2007.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest 1962 body first, then arrange the three later bodies by year.
accepted.sec: Authorities under wildlife and biodiversity laws  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 came into force in:
accepted.x: The Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 came into force in April 2023.
accepted.tq: Separate the year in the title from the year of commencement.
accepted.sec: Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act 2022 - key changes  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 reduced the number of schedules from:
accepted.x: The 2022 amendment reduced the number of schedules under the Act from six to four.
accepted.tq: Recall the before-and-after numerical change.
accepted.sec: Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act 2022 - key changes  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which international convention’s provisions were specifically brought into the Wildlife (Protection) Act through the 2022 amendment?
accepted.x: The 2022 amendment incorporated CITES-related provisions, including provisions concerning management and scientific authorities.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the wildlife-trade convention from other environmental treaties.
accepted.sec: Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act 2022 - key changes  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding changes made by the Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022:
1. The Centre was empowered to regulate invasive alien species.
2. State Governments may declare conservation reserves.
3. Every State is required to have a Chief Wildlife Warden.
4. Captive animals may be voluntarily surrendered without compensation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements describe changes associated with the 2022 amendment. Examples of invasive alien species include African catfish and Lantana camara.
accepted.tq: Test the complete amendment package rather than a single isolated change.
accepted.sec: Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act 2022 - key changes  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following is an example of an invasive alien species specifically associated with the 2022 wildlife amendment provisions?
accepted.x: African catfish is an example of an invasive alien species referred to in connection with the amendment. Lantana camara is another example.
accepted.tq: Separate an invasive alien species from native wildlife species.
accepted.sec: Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act 2022 - key changes  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The general penalty for violations under the amended wildlife law was raised to a fine of up to:
accepted.x: The general maximum fine was raised from Rs 25,000 to Rs 1 lakh. The specially protected animal category has a separate minimum fine provision.
accepted.tq: Compare the revised penalty with the earlier amount.
accepted.sec: Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act 2022 - key changes  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: For offences involving specially protected animals, the minimum fine under the amended provision was raised from Rs 10,000 to:
accepted.x: The minimum fine for offences involving specially protected animals was raised from Rs 10,000 to Rs 25,000.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a minimum penalty from the general maximum penalty.
accepted.sec: Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act 2022 - key changes  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a change introduced by the Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023?
o: All biodiversity offences were made criminal offences with imprisonment only
Benefit-sharing was abolished for all users
Offences were decriminalised and civil penalties were introduced
Foreign entities were exempted from NBA approval
accepted.x: The amendment decriminalised offences and introduced civil penalties. It did not abolish benefit-sharing or exempt foreign entities from prior NBA approval.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise legal-consequence change and reject extreme alternatives.
accepted.sec: Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act 2023  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following categories was exempted from benefit-sharing requirements under the Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023?
1. Registered AYUSH practitioners
2. Cultivated medicinal plants certified by Biodiversity Management Committees
3. All foreign-incorporated entities
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Registered AYUSH practitioners and BMC-certified cultivated medicinal plants received exemptions relating to benefit-sharing. Foreign-incorporated entities still require prior NBA approval.
accepted.tq: Reject the overbroad exemption extended to foreign entities.
accepted.sec: Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act 2023  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under the amended biodiversity framework, the ordinary time limit for NBA approval was reduced from 180 days to:
accepted.x: The ordinary NBA approval period was reduced from 180 days to 90 days. Applications relating to intellectual property rights continue to have a 180-day period.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the general time limit from the IPR exception.
accepted.sec: Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act 2023  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which category continues to require prior approval of the National Biodiversity Authority under the Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023?
accepted.x: Foreign nationals and foreign-incorporated entities continue to require prior NBA approval. The amendment did not remove this requirement.
accepted.tq: Use the foreign-entity approval rule as a legal-eligibility discriminator.
accepted.sec: Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act 2023  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under the Biological Diversity Rules, 2024, approximately what proportion of Access and Benefit Sharing proceeds is passed by the National Biodiversity Authority to State Biodiversity Boards?
accepted.x: The NBA passes approximately 85–90 percent of ABS proceeds to State Biodiversity Boards under the 2024 Rules.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the NBA-to-SBB share from the later allocation to source institutions and communities.
accepted.sec: Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act 2023  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under the Access and Benefit Sharing Regulations, April 2025, the share allocated to identifiable source institutions is:
accepted.x: The April 2025 ABS Regulations provide 25–40 percent for identifiable source institutions and 60–75 percent for local communities through SBBs or UTBCs.
accepted.tq: Compare the two percentage bands and assign each to the correct beneficiary.
accepted.sec: Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act 2023  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under the April 2025 Access and Benefit Sharing Regulations, local communities receive approximately:
accepted.x: Local communities receive 60–75 percent of the relevant ABS proceeds through State Biodiversity Boards or Union Territory Biodiversity Councils.
accepted.tq: Match the larger percentage band with the local-community beneficiary.
accepted.sec: Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act 2023  [other exams, GROUP-II]
